tagline: Canal-laced Delft is the city of Vermeer and blue-and-white Delftware, with a market square between two great churches and the tombs of the Dutch royal family.
overview: Delft is a small, picture-perfect city of canals, bridges and gabled houses between Rotterdam and The Hague. Its Markt is framed by the Renaissance City Hall and the New Church, whose tower can be climbed and whose crypt holds the Dutch royal family.

The painter Johannes Vermeer was born and worked here; his View of Delft and The Little Street show the city in the 1600s, and the Vermeer Centrum explains his life and techniques. The Old Church, with its leaning tower, is where Vermeer is buried.

Delft gave its name to Delftware, the blue-and-white pottery made since the 17th century, and Royal Delft still paints it by hand. Delft University of Technology is the country's largest technical university, giving the old town a young population.
